page: Google Cloud Platform tpu7-standard-4t is a specialized accelerator-optimized instance built on the tpu7 server family. It features 224 dedicated vCPUs with an x86_64 architecture paired with 464.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 2.07 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes equipped with 4 integrated Google TPU v7 accelerators designed for matrix multiplication and high-throughput tensor operations. This configuration contains no local NVMe storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on network-attached persistent storage for operating system and data requirements.

From an architectural perspective, the tpu7-standard-4t instance balances host system resources to sustain data pipelines feeding its four onboard custom Tensor Processing Units. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM resource ratio aligns with compute-heavy processing paradigms, ensuring adequate host-side preprocessing capacity before transferring tensor batches to the TPU hardware. Qualitative cost efficiency for this instance type centers around specialized domain workloads, where direct ASIC-level matrix execution offers optimized resource density compared to standard general-purpose host configurations without domain-specific coprocessors.

Tradeoffs for the tpu7-standard-4t instance include the complete absence of local NVMe SSD storage, requiring external persistent disk provision for I/O operations, as well as the specialized software toolchain necessary to compile and execute computational graphs on Google TPUs. The instance is suited for large-scale artificial intelligence tasks, deep learning training, massive neural network fine-tuning, and specialized machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform tpu7-standard-4t is an accelerator-optimized instance belonging to the tpu7 family, designed for specialized machine learning and artificial intelligence workloads. It features 224 dedicated vCPUs using x86_64 architecture, 464.0 GB of system memory (providing 2.07 GB per core), and four integrated Google TPU v7 accelerators. The instance includes no local storage, relying on external network storage for disk requirements, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With a compute-focused vCPU-to-RAM ratio and specialized tensor execution hardware, the server provides high qualitative resource density for parallel matrix operations. The primary trade-off is the requirement for cloud-attached persistent storage and specialized frameworks compatible with Google TPU chips. This server configuration is best suited for deep learning training, neural network model fine-tuning, distributed AI research, and high-throughput machine learning inference workloads.
